title: Terraform VPC Defender: unified SG/NACL/private-DNS/egress module
creator: Marco Chen
description: Goal: deliver a single, opinionated Terraform module (vpc_defender) that wires security groups, NACLs, private hosted zones, and egress policies for Redwood Private/VPC installs. The module must be composable for both cloud-managed (AWS) and future on-prem adapters, support safe upgrades, and emit observability hooks (health checks & policy drift tags). Scope: inputs for canonical SG/NACL rules, allowlists for service egress, private DNS delegation and resolver rules, outputs for vault/KMS key ARNs and audit tags. Reject: provider-specific autoscaling or routing changes beyond network security controls.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Module exposes inputs for all SG and NACL rule categories used by private product (control-plane, data-plane, admin), 2) Private DNS created and delegated with correct VPC associations; tests validate resolution to internal endpoints, 3) Egress policy supports whitelist and explicit deny-by-default fallback with configurable logging destination, 4) Upgrade path between v1->v2 preserves existing SG/NACL IDs and avoids destructive replacements by default, 5) Terraform plan outputs are human-readable and include drift/health tags, 6) End-to-end integration test passes in staging using the vpc_defender module and a small sample deployment, 7) Security review sign-off and CI policy checks green.
design_decisions: Make module opinionated: provide recommended defaults but allow overrides for edge cases
Keep SG config coalesced by logical role (control,data,admin) to reduce rule churn
Use separate NACLs per subnet-tier to allow coarse-grained egress gating
Implement private DNS via Route53 private hosted zones (AWS) with exports for on-prem adapter
Expose an 'egress_mode' var: 'whitelist' | 'discovery' | 'open' to make rollouts predictable
Avoid creating service-linked resources outside networking (no S3 buckets, no IAM roles) in first iteration
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module behind feature flag in terraform-registry-staging, 2) Run full terraform plan/apply against sandbox VPC (team infra), 3) Deploy to canary account with a single small customer-like VPC and enable egress_mode=whitelist, 4) Monitor health checks and DNS resolution for 48h, 5) Gradually flip additional Canary accounts, 6) Publish module and announce migration docs + runbook for customers and SEs.
test_plan: Unit: terraform validate & unit tests for plan-time variable defaults
Integration: apply to ephemeral account, verify SG/NACL IDs stable across module version bump
E2E: isolated staging VPC with sample workloads; verify outbound connections are blocked/allowed per policy
Chaos: introduce simulated partial apply failure to validate rollback guidance
Health checks: verify module provisions a simple HTTP/0 health endpoint (via tag) and CloudWatch/Datadog metric export hooks
implementation_notes: - Module split: modules/sg, modules/nacl, modules/private_dns, modules/egress_policy. - Use lifecycle ignore_changes for tags and description fields to avoid noisy diffs. - Add explicit 'preserve_existing_security_objects' boolean that defaults to true to avoid replacement on upgrade. - Provide examples for 'new install' vs 'migrate existing' flows. - Keep provider blocks minimal and documented; avoid multiple provider aliases in public examples.
